purpose: C14 seed for help-over-selling coordination: file-based asks and offers that can be published, forked, and answered without accounts or a live database.
principles: templates are not live help claims
no private contact details in public files
asks and offers point back to sourced guides, categories, or initiatives
a relay may move the file but must not become the authority

publication.relay: static host, repository discussion, or other dumb relay
publication.privacy: Do not publish private contact details, exact addresses, beneficiary identities, or sensitive threat models in this file.

items.title: We need help running a digital-safety clinic
items.summary: A library, community group, or mutual-aid group needs help with safer messaging, passwords, 2FA, VPN basics, and a handout people can actually use.
items.prompt: Can you help run a calm digital-safety session for people who do not want jargon?

receipts.note: EFF publishes Surveillance Self-Defense as public digital-security guidance for people and groups.
Library Freedom Project publishes resources for privacy and intellectual freedom work in libraries.

limits: Do not publish a group's threat model or participant names.
Do not imply the facilitator can provide legal or emergency safety advice.

items.title: I can share a private-communications starter pack
items.summary: I can share a plain-language checklist for moving a group to Signal, choosing a password manager, and setting safer admin habits.
items.prompt: I can share a starter pack for safer group communication and help adapt it to your group's constraints.

receipts.note: Signal publishes support material for group chats and group-management features.
Access Now runs digital-security and digital-rights support programs for at-risk users and civil society.

limits: Do not post invite links publicly.
Do not turn the offer into private security consulting without consent and scope.

items.title: We need help checking a fundraiser before we share it
items.summary: A local group wants a quick accountability check before amplifying a fundraiser or emergency giving appeal.
items.prompt: Can you help us check the organizer identity, payment route, recipient clarity, fees, and update pattern before we share this?

receipts.note: The FTC's charity guidance tells donors to check charity names, payment methods, and fundraiser claims before giving.
BBB Wise Giving Alliance publishes charity accountability standards that can inform lightweight due-diligence checks.

limits: Do not publish recipient medical, immigration, housing, or safety details.
Do not present a quick check as a formal audit.

items.title: I can share a one-page giving research brief
items.summary: I can make a short source list for people comparing evidence-backed giving, climate giving, or local commitments before a fundraising season.
items.prompt: I can turn public giving research into a one-page brief that keeps impact, transparency, and local commitments separate.

receipts.note: GiveWell publishes a top-charities list and research pages for highly cost-effective giving opportunities.
Giving What We Can publishes cause-area guidance for donors comparing global health, animal welfare, climate, and other areas.

limits: Do not imply the brief is personal financial, tax, or legal advice.
Do not collapse local relationship-based giving into cost-effectiveness scoring.

items.title: We need help choosing a repair-first phone or laptop
items.summary: A household, school, or small organization wants to compare repair, reuse, refurbished options, software support, and total cost before buying.
items.prompt: Can you help us compare repairability, software support, used or refurbished options, and total cost before we replace devices?

receipts.note: iFixit publishes repairability material for electronics, including phones and laptops.
The FTC's Nixing the Fix report describes repair restrictions as a consumer and competition issue.

limits: Do not ask volunteers to handle devices containing private data without a wipe plan.
Do not present repairability as a substitute for safety recalls or warranty rights.

items.title: I can help a nonprofit map open-source and security-maintenance options
items.summary: I can help a nonprofit compare maintainable open-source tools, hosted options, security responsibilities, and exit plans before it gets locked in.
items.prompt: I can help compare open-source tools, security-maintenance responsibilities, hosted options, and exit plans for a nonprofit workflow.

receipts.note: OpenSSF coordinates industry and community work on open-source software security.
TechSoup provides nonprofit technology resources, discounts, and learning material.

limits: Do not collect sensitive beneficiary data while scoping tool needs.
Do not recommend self-hosting unless the group has maintenance capacity.
